claims.proposition: In a DAG, nodes represent variables, arrows represent proposed directions, and paths are connected routes through arrows.

resources.text: A city team records households' voluntary use of a water-filter app, later illness-related absences, and a DAG proposed to explain the pattern. Which conclusion is justified without adding an assumption?
Separate the recorded pattern from the proposed DAG and from what would happen if the city deliberately assigned use of the app.
The records establish an association. The DAG is a model with explicit causal assumptions, and an intervention would require deliberately assigning use rather than only observing voluntary choices.
Correct choice on this delayed association-versus-causation check. This is one classification decision, not evidence of mastery across the nine M0 concepts.
That conclusion treats an observed pattern and a model drawing as if they already proved an intervention effect. They are different kinds of information.

choices.text: The records support an association; causal direction and an intervention effect still require explicit assumptions or interventional evidence.
Because voluntary app users had fewer absences, assigning the app to other households would reduce their absences.
